_about: Public-domain James Caughey (1810?-1891), Irish-born American Methodist revivalist in Canada and Britain, for the Word Hoard: Letters on Various Subjects, Methodism in Earnest, Helps to a Life of Holiness and Usefulness (Revival Miscellanies), The Triumph of Truth, Showers of Blessing, Arrows from my Quiver, Glimpses of Life in Soul-saving, and Light in the Dark. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 103 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

caughey-methodism-earnest: Methodism in earnest: being the history of a great revival in Great Britain; in which twenty thousand souls were justified, and ten thousand sanctified, in about six years, through the instrumentality of Rev. James Caughey; including an account of the mental and spiritual exercises which made him so eminent a revivalist (Boston, C. H. Peirce, 1850)
caughey-revival-miscellanies: Revival miscellanies, containing eleven revival sermons : and thoughts on entire sanctification (Boston : For sale by J.P. Magee, 1851)
caughey-helps-holiness: Helps to a life of holiness and usefulness (Boston, J. P. Magee, agent, 1852)
caughey-triumph-truth: The triumph of truth, and continental letters and sketches, from the journal, letters, and sermons of the Rev. James Caughey (New York Carlton & Porter, 1857)
caughey-showers-blessing: Showers of blessing from clouds of mercy (Boston, J. P. Magee, 1860)
caughey-arrows: Arrows from my quiver (New York, W. C. Palmer, jr., 1867)
caughey-glimpses: Glimpses of life in soul-saving (New York, W. C. Palmer, jr., 1868)
caughey-light-in-dark: Light in the dark, through the dominions Unbelief (W. C. Palmer, 1868)

_excluded.caughey-memoir: A Brief Memoir... of the Rev. J. Caughey (by another hand)
